Apps
No apps yet. Webxdc apps are small offline apps (games, polls, checklists, editors) in a single .xdc file: get them from webxdc.org/apps and install them here. Pandora can use them with you: she reads what happens in an app and can send her own moves, and she can build new apps in the vault and install them.
Schedules

Runs a prompt, a shell command or a ritual on a schedule, in your local time. From the shell: crontab -l. Schedules fire only while this app is open; a run missed while it was closed can catch up once when you return.

New schedule
Runs in the shell on its own (no chat, no model). Output goes to /Pandora/Logs/cron.log; a failure notifies you.

Model provider
If it fails, try these in order
Used when the provider can't be reached, times out, or hits a rate limit. Pandora switches back automatically when it returns.

Ollama must allow this page's origin. Start it with OLLAMA_ORIGINS="*" ollama serve (or set the variable in the Ollama app's environment and restart it). Pick a model with tool support, such as qwen3, gpt-oss, llama3.1 or mistral-small.

MCP servers

Works like pi: servers live in Pandora/mcp.json and connect in the background. codemode (default) keeps their tools out of the prompt; Pandora writes a short script that calls them. deferred loads tools on demand with tool_search, direct shows them like built-in tools, hidden turns them off. Streamable HTTP servers only; a stdio server needs an HTTP bridge such as npx -y supergateway --stdio "…" --outputTransport streamableHttp.

Add a server
Heartbeat

Every so often Pandora wakes up, reads Pandora/HEARTBEAT.md and checks what it lists. If all is well she answers HEARTBEAT_OK and stays quiet; otherwise you get a notification. An empty checklist costs nothing.

Background

The app shows a small notification while it keeps Pandora alive. Android needs that to let her finish work with the screen off.

In a browser tab, Pandora keeps working while the tab stays open, but the browser may slow it down in the background. Install the Android app for real background runs.

Backup

Export to a JSON file. Everything = all leaves and files, chats, schedules, memory, skills and settings. Config = settings, SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, SYSTEM.md, memory and skills. Import a file to restore it: a full backup replaces what is here, a config file merges in.

Persona, instructions & skills

SOUL.md is who Pandora is. AGENTS.md holds your standing instructions. SYSTEM.md (optional) replaces her base prompt. All three are leaves, read fresh on every message; text inside <!-- comments --> is not sent.

Skills · run with /skill:name, or Pandora picks them
Long-term memory

Pandora keeps what she learns about you in the leaf Pandora/Memory and reads it at the start of every chat. When you leave a chat (or after a few quiet minutes) she writes a short entry in her quest log under Pandora/Journal and adds new facts to memory. Both are plain leaves you can edit or delete.

History compaction

Long chats overflow the model's context window. Compaction has the model summarise the older turns; from then on it sees the summary instead of them. The full history stays visible here.

A small, fast model is usually enough for summaries and saves your main model's time. If it fails, the chat model is used. A turn is one message from you plus everything the agent does in reply. Type /compact to compact now.

Trajectory log (fine-tuning data)

Records every agent run exactly as the model saw it: system prompt, tools, your messages, its replies, tool calls and results. It stays on this device until you export it as JSONL for fine-tuning your own model. Rate replies with 👍 / 👎 in the chat to choose what goes in.

Text & layout
Scales the whole interface, on this device.

With room to spare the Atelier widens; drag the handles beside it to set its width. When it is wide, Leaves shows the list beside the open leaf and Chat puts Pandora beside the conversation, each with a divider to drag. The editor's Split mode and Pandora's height (on a phone) drag too. Double-click a handle to reset it. Your layout is kept with your settings.

Pandora companion

Voices come from your browser and operating system, so the list differs between machines. British female voices are picked first when set to Auto. Pandora lip-syncs to whatever voice you choose.

Ollaya decisions

Ollaya runs decision models locally. It doesn't write text: it answers questions you define with calibrated probabilities. When it's on, the agent gets a decide tool for triage, classification, scoring and yes/no checks. Ollama still does the chatting.


        
Install from ollaya.dev, then run ollaya serve and pull a model (for example ollaya pull winnow:e4b). It accepts requests from localhost and local files by default. For the hosted page, start it with OLLAYA_ORIGINS="*" ollaya serve.

      


      

        
BusyBox WASM

        
BusyBox 1.37 is built into this page. Each applet runs as a fresh WebAssembly instance in a worker, on a copy of the virtual filesystem that is written back when it exits. Pipes, redirects, sh -c and xargs are handled by the page's own shell, because WebAssembly cannot fork.

Leaf scripts & templates

        
Leaves can run JavaScript like Obsidian's Dataview and Templater: ```dataviewjs (or ```jade-js) blocks and inline `$= …` show live results in Read view, and leaves in your templates folder fill in <% tp.date.now() %> tags when you insert them with the { } button in the editor. Scripts run sandboxed: they read the Atelier, with no network and no file changes.

        
        
        

      


      

        
API endpoint

        
Let other apps and scripts talk to Pandora. They send a GET request and get JSON back. A message sent this way goes through the normal chat: it appears in the app and Pandora answers there.

        

          
          

            

            

          

          

            

          

          
Try it

          
Request and reply format

GET /v1/chat?message=TEXT
  session=new | CHAT_ID   start a new chat or continue one
                          (default: the chat open in the app)
  wait=0                  answer 202 at once; poll /v1/status,
                          then read /v1/history
  tools=0                 leave tool_calls out of the reply
  timeout=SECONDS         how long to wait (default 300, max 1800)
  json={"message":"hi","new":true}
                          the same parameters as one JSON object

Reply: {"ok":true,"api":1,"reply":"...",
  "session":{"id","title","messages"},
  "tool_calls":[{"name","arguments","ok","result"}],
  "model","elapsed_ms","error":null}

GET /v1/status   busy flag, model, open chat
GET /v1/history?limit=20&session=CHAT_ID
GET /v1/chats    list of chats
GET /v1/health   no token needed

Errors: {"ok":false,"error":{"code","message"}} with HTTP
400 bad request, 401 token, 404 unknown chat, 409 busy,
502 model error, 504 timeout (Jade keeps going in the app).

Send the token as  Authorization: Bearer TOKEN  or  ?token=TOKEN.
Over Wi-Fi the traffic is plain HTTP, so use a trusted network.

        

        
The API runs inside the Android app. A browser tab cannot listen for requests.

      


      

        
Vector messenger (Pandora as a bot)

        
Pandora lives on Vector as a bot account: she answers DMs and channels, reacts, sends files, sees images, plays Mini Apps, joins and leaves communities, and takes messages for you. Vector itself runs in the Pandora's Vector bridge on a computer that stays on (Mac, Linux or Docker: see the pandora-vector folder), and this app connects to it like it does to Ollama.

        
        

        

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

        

        
        
        

        
You (her Partner) get the same Pandora as in this app, with every tool. Admins get Vector powers but never your leaves, memory or files. Everyone else can chat, play Mini Apps and leave you messages. Each Vector chat has its own chat here (💬). Keep the app running for her to answer: Config → Background mode keeps it alive on Android.

      


      

        
Discord (Pandora as a bot)

        
Pandora lives on Discord as a bot: she answers DMs and channels, reacts, sends files, sees images, and takes messages for you. It works at the same time as Vector. The bot runs in the Pandora's Discord bridge (pandora-discord/, built on discord.py) on a computer you keep on; paste its URL and token here. Create the bot at discord.com/developers/applications → Bot, give its token to the bridge (--set-token), and turn on Message Content Intent. Then use Copy invite link and open it to add her to your server.

        
        

        

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

          

        

        
        

        
You (her Partner) get the same Pandora as in this app, with every tool. Admins get Discord powers but never your leaves, memory or files. Everyone else can chat and leave you messages. Each Discord chat has its own chat here (🎮). Jade never pings @everyone or roles, and ignores other bots. Vector and Discord share one Jade: she answers one conversation at a time. Keep the app running for her to answer: Config → Background mode keeps it alive on Android.

      


      

        
Secrets (API keys for Pandora's HTTP requests)

        
Pandora writes {{NAME}} in a URL, header or body and the app fills in the value when the request goes out. She never sees the value, so it stays out of chats, the trajectory log and replies (any echo is blanked). Node scripts get them as process.env.NAME.
